summary: The sm_90a build fix is correct and the rewrite is worth re-running as stage 1, but the spec also requires the self-check to run in a spawned child process, and TASK.md rejects any submission that 'starts processes' (a spawn context also re-imports the harness __main__), so hold until that sub-change is removed or replaced with an in-process canary.
justification: Design (a kind: rewrite, so judged on its replaced-kernel rows, not the headline): sound for H200 at these shapes. Master spends 292.5 us at bs=128 and 391.4 us at bs=256 in Marlin, which is 95% of each shape and 2.9x / 3.6x the 101.3 / 108.9 us floors, about 1.5 and 1.1 TB/s effective. At bs=256, roughly 350-450 local routes x 2 GEMMs is tens of us of BF16 MMA even at wgmma peak, so the argument that an mma.sync engine plus dequant cannot get near the floor holds, and wgmma with a register-A dequantized weight (swap-AB, weight rows on M) is the right tensor-core path. The bytes-in-flight plan (>= 48 KB of weight per SM across 5-6 stages, bulk copy plus TMA, 1 producer and 2 consumer warpgroups) is the right order of magnitude for ~3 TB/s. The register budget is legal: 40x128 + 232x256 = 64512 <= 65536. The control shapes (bs<128) are gated off and correctly expected flat. The build diagnosis is also correct: per REWRITE_READ section 3 and LESSONS 2026-10-25, cpp_extension added a compute_90 pass, and pinning TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=9.0a with only -gencode compute_90a/sm_90a plus the __CUDA_ARCH_FEAT_SM90_ALL guard is the documented fix. Weakest link: no instruction in this kernel has ever executed on the judge. The archived patch keeps createpolicy.fractional.L2::evict_first/evict_normal and an L2::cache_hint variant of cp.async.bulk (patch lines ~160 and ~447). The sibling swap-AB kernel trapped with illegal instruction 715, and LESSONS names that exact helper family as the prime suspect. Applying the kernel 'verbatim' therefore carries the most likely fault forward, along with setmaxnreg, mbarrier expect_tx, TMA tensor-map encoding through cudaGetDriverEntryPoint, and stmatrix.trans, all first executions. Second risk: compile time. Two families x four N buckets of a wgmma template has never compiled on the judge (the first attempt died in ptxas), so it is unknown whether it fits the 15-minute run budget alongside prepare's 300 s.
confounders: align-parallel-per-expert-verify (master tip): the archived wgmma path calls moe_align_block_size(local_ids, 16, 32) at num_tokens >= 128, so on the target shapes it bypasses master's _align_parallel_kernel (4.0 / 6.9 us). Compare the replaced-kernel rows only (gather + w13 + w2 against Marlin x2 + act_and_mul) and report align separately, or the align delta of a few us leaks into the shape row. The rebase onto align-parallel must state which align the wgmma branch uses.

marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm / triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack: they set block_size_m for Marlin at bs>=128, which only shapes the incumbent row (292.5 / 391.4 us). The wgmma path uses its own block 16, so this is no confound on the kernel row, but the M2 incumbent must be read from the same run's base profile, not the 316.1 / 490.2 us quoted from an older base.
post-expert-norm-triton-small-m: no interaction. bs>=32 still calls SGLang's fused_post_expert_norm_weighted_sum, and the wgmma w2 epilogue scatters into cache3 in the layout that combine expects.
sglang-marlin-path-parity: this is the fallback path itself, so a run without PATH CHOSEN = WGMMA measures parity/master again, which the spec already labels unmeasured.
interference: No companion is warranted. As a rewrite it is judged on its own kernel rows (gather + w13 + w2 at bs=128/256) against the same run's Marlin + act_and_mul rows and the floor. The bs<128 shapes are built-in controls. Marlin's ±20% profile noise affects only the incumbent reference, and the ~2x gap to M3 is far larger than that. An ab-revert of any landed hypothesis would not change attribution, because the replaced kernels are disjoint from everything landed except the align call noted above, which should be reported, not A/B'd. The next stage is the follow-up.
rules_flags: STARTS PROCESSES: the spec runs the setup self-check 'in a spawned child process'. TASK.md says 'A submission is rejected if it ... starts processes'. A multiprocessing spawn child also re-imports the parent's __main__ (the judge's harness), which risks the 'reads harness frames / touches harness I/O' clause and could re-execute harness code. load_inline's own nvcc/ninja invocation is the sanctioned exception, and an explicit Python child process is not covered by it. Remove it. Alternatives: (a) accept that a sticky fault costs one check run, since this is a check-mode rewrite stage; (b) do an in-process canary launch first with -lineinfo and CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING-free cudaGetLastError plus a torch.cuda.synchronize in prepare (allowed, untimed), and accept that a trap kills the run; (c) reduce trap probability by replacing the createpolicy/L2::cache_hint bulk copy with the plain cp.async.bulk...mbarrier::complete_tx::bytes form (no cache_hint operand).

Same flag applies to the queued sibling cuda-nvfp4-swapab-mma-persistent-small-m-childcheck (multiprocessing spawn) and to LESSONS 2026-10-25's 'run the first launch in a child process' advice. Both need the same correction.

Otherwise clean: NVFP4 weights repacked losslessly (round-trip assert), BF16 activations, fp32 accumulation, scratch buffers overwritten every call with nothing derived from data cached, the gate branches only on num_tokens and a prepare-time flag, no host syncs in kernel_fn, and setting and restoring TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST in-process is fine.
open_questions: Rebase target: if stack-onewarp-hoisted-dispatchcombine(-from17), now running, lands first, it changes align and combine at bs>=128. Keep the wgmma gate on its own WG_MIN_TOKENS constant as the spec says, and confirm the w2 scatter still matches the new combine's input layout.

Should the 'verbatim' kernel keep createpolicy + L2::cache_hint on cp.async.bulk, given that LESSONS names cache-hint helpers as the prime 715 suspect? Dropping the hint costs little (weights are streamed once) and removes the most likely trap.
Will the build fit the 15-minute run limit? Log compile seconds, and consider trimming to the N buckets that bs=128/256/257 actually hit.
The log string is 'PATH CHOSEN = WGMMA' (uppercase) in the patch, and the harvest grep should match it case-insensitively.
